msg: PackageLicenseUrl is deprecated (NU5125: "The 'licenseUrl' element will be deprecated. Consider using the 'license' element instead."). Use PackageLicenseExpression or PackageLicenseFile instead.

PackageIconUrl without PackageIcon raises NU5048: "The 'PackageIconUrl'/'iconUrl' element is deprecated. Consider using the 'PackageIcon'/'icon' element instead." Embed the icon (PNG or JPEG, 1 MB max, 128x128 recommended). Keeping PackageIconUrl next to PackageIcon is fine for older clients.
PackageLicenseExpression must be an SPDX license identifier or expression (NuGet's ABNF: identifiers joined by AND, OR, WITH, optional +). This value is not a valid SPDX expression.
nuget.org "only accepts license expressions that are approved by the Open Source Initiative or the Free Software Foundation". This identifier is neither, so use a packed licence file instead.
"Only one of PackageLicenseExpression, PackageLicenseFile, and PackageLicenseUrl can be specified at a time." This project sets PackageLicenseExpression and PackageLicenseFile.
fix: keep one: PackageLicenseExpression (SPDX licence) or PackageLicenseFile (custom licence)

msg: PackageLicenseFile points to a file that no item in this project packs. "You need to explicitly pack the referenced license file."

PackageIcon points to a file that no item in this project packs, or to a format NuGet does not take. "You need to explicitly pack the referenced icon image file"; supported formats are JPEG and PNG, 1 MB max.

PackageReadmeFile points to a file that no item in this project packs, or that is not Markdown. "You need to explicitly pack the referenced readme file"; "Supported file formats include only Markdown (.md)".
Microsoft's .NET support policy lists .NET 8 (LTS) and .NET 9 (STS) with end of support on November 10, 2026. After that date they get no more patches.
This target framework is no longer on Microsoft's list of supported .NET versions (only .NET 8, 9 and 10 are). A new package version that targets it ships on an unpatched runtime.
